issues.issue: Fix (a) computes `innerSafe = isCompatibilitySelectionSafe(projection.getArg())`, i.e. selection-safety of the Projection's ARGUMENT only. But the parser puts Slice ABOVE the Projection for sub-selects (LateralQueryEvaluationStep.java:159-165 walks Slice/Order/Distinct/Reduced down to the Projection; FilterIterator.java:446-475 today checks safety from the sub-select ROOT so a Slice makes the body unsafe). With the design, `{ SELECT ?t ?x WHERE { ?t :r ?x } ORDER BY ?x LIMIT 1 }` has arg Order(SP) -> 'safe' -> projected ?x is pre-bound -> LIMIT is applied AFTER the selection = substitution semantics, not the bottom-up semantics the design says it implements. Concrete mis-evaluation through the containsSubquery-stops-at-Join hole the design itself identifies (TupleExprs.java:57-62; LeftJoin right arg Join(Slice(Projection),SP) is NOT out-of-scope, so LeftJoinIterator.java:94-103 -> JoinIterator evaluates the sub-select with the left row): data `:a :p 2 . :c :r 1 . :d :r 2 . :d :z :y1`, query `SELECT * { ?s :p ?x OPTIONAL { { SELECT ?t ?x WHERE { ?t :r ?x } ORDER BY ?x LIMIT 1 } ?t :z ?y } }`. SPARQL 1.1 bottom-up: sub-select = {t=c,x=1}, `?t :z ?y` fails for c, result {s=a,x=2}. Design: x=2 pushed -> {t=d,x=2} -> LIMIT 1 -> join succeeds -> {s=a,x=2,t=d,y=y1}. Wrong. The same mechanics also make the design's own stated 'compatibility' choice for EXISTS over a LIMIT sub-select false in practice (it would get substitution), so the 'pin with a test' item would immediately contradict the design text.
issues.suggestion: Decide selection-safety on the whole sub-select unit: from the Projection walk up through Distinct/Reduced/Order parents; any Slice above the Projection => not selection-safe (Distinct/Reduced/Order commute with a selection on projected names; Slice does not). Better: do not pre-bind by correlation at all in a nested Projection (withhold every incoming binding except LATERAL-substituted names, which are constants by definition) and implement EXISTS's projected-variable substitution explicitly in the scoped substitution visitor (see 3.4.3 major). Add the counter-example above as a memory e2e test and a ProjectionQueryEvaluationStep unit test with Slice(Projection(Order(SP))) receiving a projected binding.

issues.issue: The design picks 'independent evaluation + compatibility' for EXISTS over a non-monotone sub-select whose PROJECTED variable is bound in the outer row, flagged as an open question. The SPARQL EXISTS CG report that SPARQL 1.2 builds on defines exists(X) = eval(Replace(PrjMap(X), mu)) where PrjMap renames every sub-query variable NOT in the projection to a fresh variable (bottom-up, before evaluation) and projected variables ARE restricted to the outer row's values inside the sub-select, i.e. before LIMIT/aggregation (fetched from w3c.github.io/sparql-exists; the W3C sparql12-query page was truncated before section 18 so the final text could not be quoted). Under that semantics `SELECT ?s { ?s :p ?x FILTER EXISTS { SELECT ?x WHERE { ?t :r ?x } ORDER BY ?x LIMIT 1 } }` with data `:a :p 2 . :c :r 1 . :d :r 2` is TRUE (x:=2 inside, `?t :r 2` has a row), while the design's compatibility rule evaluates unbound, gets {x=1}, and returns FALSE. Combined with the blocker above, the design would give substitution for LIMIT (accidentally) and compatibility for aggregates (Group is below the Projection), an incoherent mix.
issues.suggestion: Implement EXISTS substitution per the spec text in the new scoped substitution visitor (3.4.3(b)): descend into Projection/MultiProjection but replace only Vars whose name is a projected SOURCE name of that projection (and not shadowed by an inner projection); leave non-projected Vars untouched (fresh by construction). Then the runtime ProjectionQueryEvaluationStep boundary can be purely bottom-up (withhold all non-LATERAL incoming bindings), which is exactly right for OPTIONAL/Join correlation, and the `Exists` holder trick (c) becomes unnecessary because EXISTS no longer relies on runtime pass-through. Confirm against the final SPARQL 1.2 section 18 'Substitute' definition before landing and pin both a LIMIT and a GROUP BY/HAVING case in tests.

issues.issue: `isOutOfScopeForCorrelation(rightArg)` includes `TupleExprs.isVariableScopeChange(rightArg)`. The parser marks EVERY `{A} UNION {B}` Union as a variable scope change (TupleExprBuilder.java:1548; only path-alternative unions are cleared at :1625; ASTUnionGraphPattern.java:20 is the only AST node that sets isScopeChange, so OPTIONAL groups are not flagged), the normalizer preserves the flag (QueryModelNormalizerOptimizer.java:79,87) and the packed materializer restores it (PackedPlanMaterializer.java:942). Therefore every `OPTIONAL { {A} UNION {B} }` would hit the new FIRST branch of supply and run an UNBOUNDED HashJoinIteration, pre-empting the memoized path (LeftJoinQueryEvaluationStep.java:102-113) and the bounded AdaptiveHashLeftJoinIteration with LeftJoinIterator fallback (:114-129, MaterializationLimitExceededException at :513, BoundedHashJoinIteration :665-687). Union is compatibility-selection-safe, so correlation is sound for it; the flag is about BIND/FILTER visibility, not correlation. The unit tests will not catch this because `new Union(...)` in LeftJoinQueryEvaluationStepTest.java:159 and :417 leaves the flag false, and the memory guard `adaptiveHashOptionalFallbackKeepsResults` still returns correct rows while silently no longer exercising the bounded path.
issues.suggestion: Use `containsSubquery(rightArg) || containsDifferenceInCurrentScope(rightArg) || (isVariableScopeChange(rightArg) && !isCompatibilitySelectionSafe(rightArg))` for the LeftJoin out-of-scope predicate (or order the new branch after the memoized/adaptive branches for scope-change-only right args). Add a LeftJoinQueryEvaluationStepTest variant that calls `union.setVariableScopeChange(true)` and asserts the adaptive/bounded algorithm is still chosen.

issues.issue: The minus-mode branch is placed inside supplyMaterializedExistsSemiJoin AFTER decline paths that return null, and FilterIterator.supply (FilterIterator.java:28-58) then falls through to the plain FilterIterator whose `Not(Exists)` condition is compiled via DefaultEvaluationStrategy.prepare(Exists) (:2112-2129) -> existsProbeFunction -> NOT EXISTS substitution semantics for a MINUS-derived node. Paths that bypass the design's branch: (i) `filter.isVariableScopeChange()` decline (:232-233); (ii) `isPartOfSubQuery(filter)` decline (:235-236) — isPartOfSubQuery means 'has an Exists/SubQueryValueOperator ancestor' (:861-871), so a hinted anti-join inside an EXISTS body is always declined; (iii) `planned-streaming-exists` hint (:229-230); (iv) `supplyFilteredBindingSetAssignmentJoin` runs BEFORE the semi-join supply (:32-35) and fuses Filter(Join(X, VALUES), cond) whenever VarNameCollector over the condition (which descends into the Exists body) intersects the VALUES names — a MINUS with a VALUES left operand would be evaluated as NOT EXISTS; (v) the planner's plain-FILTER alternative also carries `optimizer.semiAntiKind=minus-assured-shared` (PackedCostSession.java:490-495) but not necessarily an algorithm hint, so `explicitlyPlanned=false` and `!subqueryVarReferencesAreOutputs` (:261-263, true for the repro body `?s :q ?v FILTER(?v=?o)`) declines it -> plain FilterIterator -> NOT EXISTS. The design's guard is therefore too narrow: it only protects the one path that reaches line 249.
issues.suggestion: Read `optimizer.semiAntiKind` at the very top of FilterIterator.supply (before the fused-BSA path and before any decline) and, when it is `minus-assured-shared`, either build the validated minus-mode MaterializedExistsFilterIteration or return `bs -> new MinusQueryEvaluationStep(arg, existsArg, filter.getArg(), subQuery).evaluate(bs)`; never let such a Filter reach the generic FilterIterator/ExistsQueryValueEvaluationStep. Add tests for the hinted filter (a) with isVariableScopeChange=true, (b) nested inside an EXISTS body, (c) with a VALUES left operand, (d) with the kind but no algorithm hint.

issues.issue: The residual predicate reuses `ScopedQueryValueEvaluationStep(leftJoin.getBindingNames(), condition)`, which rebuilds the binding set from the scope names only (ScopedQueryValueEvaluationStep.java:29-45) and therefore hides LATERAL-substituted inputs that are in scope by substitution. Pre-existing in the PostFilter/PreFilter steps (LeftJoinQueryEvaluationStep.java:740-758): for `?s :p ?o LATERAL { OPTIONAL { ?s :q ?y FILTER(?y = ?o) } }` the LeftJoin is LeftJoin(SingletonSet, SP) with binding names {s,y}; `?o` is dropped from the condition's scope -> ValueExprEvaluationException -> false -> the OPTIONAL never matches (data `:a :p :o1 . :a :q :o1` should yield {s=a,o=o1,y=o1}). The hash residual would bake the same bug into the new path.
issues.suggestion: Scope the condition to `leftJoin.getBindingNames() ∪ BindingScopeAnalysis.lateralSubstitutedNames(leftJoin)` in determineRightEvaluationStep and in the new residual; add a LateralQueryEvaluationStepTest e2e for the query above.

issues.issue: The soundness argument ('pushing exactly the comparison names is a selection') only holds when the pushed name is ASSURED on the right operand. comparisonBindingNames are shared OUTPUT names (MinusQueryEvaluationStep.java:104-137, via getBindingNames, which includes OPTIONAL-produced names). Counter-example under any correlated caller: l={s=a,y=y1}, R = `?s :a ?b OPTIONAL { ?s :c ?y }`, data `:a :a :b . :a :c :y2`. Bottom-up R={s=a,b,y=y2}: incompatible on y, l kept. With {s,y=y1} pushed: the inner LeftJoin sees y as a problem var, BadlyDesignedLeftJoinIterator.java:84-106 evaluates without y, gets {s=a,b,y=y2}, rejects it as incompatible and (join 'succeeded') emits nothing... but for a subject with NO :c edge the unmatched row {s=a,b} is EXTENDED with y=y1 (:94-100) -> R'={s=a,b,y=y1} -> compatible -> l wrongly removed. After 3.4.1 plus the Join guard (JoinQueryEvaluationStep.java:80,164-177) the only remaining correlated pushes into a Difference are LATERAL/EXISTS, where substitution semantics make the push correct, so this is latent — but the design text claims general soundness and FedX/direct callers can still correlate.
issues.suggestion: Push `comparisonBindingNames ∩ rightArg.getAssuredBindingNames()` plus LATERAL-substituted names; state in the Javadoc that the general guarantee comes from 3.4.1/Join routing, not from this restriction.

issues.issue: `lateralSubstitutedNames` is derived statically from `lateral.getRightInputBindingNames()` (= enclosing lateral inputs + left binding names, TupleExprBuilder.java:3266-3277), but at runtime only names actually bound in the current left row are substituted (LateralQueryEvaluationStep.java:127-135 skips unbound ones). When the Lateral's left arg binds ?s optionally and an enclosing correlated operator supplies ?s through originalBindings, the LeftJoin would treat that correlation binding as substituted and skip the bottom-up (badly-designed) handling. Narrow but a real divergence between the static analysis and the runtime substitution.
issues.suggestion: Either document the assumption, or intersect the static set with the Lateral's assured left binding names, or have LateralQueryEvaluationStep pass the actually-substituted names per row (e.g. via the synthetic parent it already creates).

issues.issue: `isNestedProjection` allowlists QueryRoot/Slice/Distinct/Reduced/Order/DescribeOperator as non-nesting ancestors, but the packed materializer can emit `MaterializeTupleExpr` as a unary wrapper (PackedPlanMaterializer.java:180-181; PackedJoinEnumerator.java:2357 treats MATERIALIZE like QUERY_ROOT/PROJECTION/ORDER). If it sits above a top-level Projection, that projection would be misclassified as nested and would withhold external bindings from FedX/direct callers. Also ProjectionIterator.determineOuterProjection (ProjectionIterator.java:107-114) uses a different nested-ness notion (has a Projection/MultiProjection ancestor), so the two disagree for the EXISTS clone and for Join/LeftJoin-nested sub-selects.
issues.suggestion: Add MaterializeTupleExpr to the allowlist (or define 'nested' as having a binary-operator/Exists/Lateral ancestor) and make ProjectionIterator use the same BindingScopeAnalysis predicate.

issues.issue: existingTestsAtRisk is incomplete: `LeftJoinQueryEvaluationStepTest#positiveUnionOptionalFallsBackWhenHashBuildExceedsLimit` (:410-447, asserts LeftJoinIterator fallback) and `#unionOptionalDeclinesIndependentEvaluationForBadlyDesignedInput` (:512) stay green only because their Unions lack the parser's scope-change flag; the e2e behaviour they protect is what the Union routing issue above changes. Also HashJoinIteration.getNextElement returns `EmptyBindingSet.getInstance()` at :261 when no candidates remain; the residual-loop rewrite must preserve the LookAheadIteration null-on-exhaustion contract and keep counting rejected candidates in hashCandidateRows for cost feedback.
issues.suggestion: Add scope-flagged Union variants of both tests and a HashJoinIterationTest for the residual path asserting termination and counters.

missedFindings: LATERAL condition scoping (executor, pre-existing, not in REVIEW 3.4/3.9): OPTIONAL conditions inside a LATERAL right arg are evaluated with ScopedQueryValueEvaluationStep(leftJoin.getBindingNames()) (LeftJoinQueryEvaluationStep.java:740-758, ScopedQueryValueEvaluationStep.java:29-45), which strips lateral-substituted inputs, e.g. `?s :p ?o LATERAL { OPTIONAL { ?s :q ?y FILTER(?y = ?o) } }` never matches. The design's residual copies this scope.

Nested ProjectionIterator overwrites conflicting parent bindings instead of rejecting the row: includeAllParentBindings path starts from `context.createBindingSet(parentBindings)` and applies `bs.setBinding` (ProjectionIterator.java:64-100; QueryEvaluationContext.java:214-215), so a nested sub-select row with x=2 under a parent x=1 yields x=2 today. The design's compatibility filter fixes it implicitly; it should be named and tested as its own defect.

FedX (tools/federation/FederationEvaluationStrategy.java:810-830) has its own copy of the `!hasCondition() && containsSubquery` gate with a correlated fallback for conditioned OPTIONAL-over-sub-select, i.e. the 3.4.1 shape exists in FedX independently of LeftJoinQueryEvaluationStep; the design only lists FedX for HashJoinIteration constructor compatibility.

3.4.4 guard placement (see issue): the hinted anti-join can reach the generic FilterIterator/ExistsQueryValueEvaluationStep via the fused BindingSetAssignment join (FilterIterator.java:32-35), the scope-change/isPartOfSubQuery/planned-streaming declines (:229-236) and the hint-less FILTER-form alternative (:261-263); the review and design both treat supplyMaterializedExistsSemiJoin as the single entry point.
semanticRegressionRisks: Wrong results (3.4.3 as designed): `SELECT * { ?s :p ?x OPTIONAL { { SELECT ?t ?x WHERE { ?t :r ?x } ORDER BY ?x LIMIT 1 } ?t :z ?y } }` with `:a :p 2 . :c :r 1 . :d :r 2 . :d :z :y1` returns {s=a,x=2,t=d,y=y1} instead of {s=a,x=2}, because the Slice above the Projection is ignored when deciding to pre-bind projected names.

Spec divergence (3.4.3 as designed): `FILTER EXISTS { SELECT ?x WHERE { ?t :r ?x } ORDER BY ?x LIMIT 1 }` with outer x=2 and data `:c :r 1 . :d :r 2` is TRUE under the CG-report/SPARQL 1.2 substitution (values injected before LIMIT) but FALSE under the design's compatibility rule; aggregates/HAVING cases diverge the same way.

Lost sound optimization + memory cliff (3.4.1): every `OPTIONAL { {A} UNION {B} }` (parser-flagged scope change) moves from the bounded AdaptiveHashLeftJoinIteration/memoized paths to an unbounded HashJoinIteration build of the whole UNION.

Lost sound optimization (3.4.1 + 3.4.2): `?s :p ?o OPTIONAL { ?s :q ?y MINUS { ?y :r ?z } }` is now materialized unbound (full `?s :q ?y` scan) although, with 3.4.2 restricted to assured comparison names, the correlated LeftJoinIterator path is sound for a Difference right arg; consider routing Difference right args to hash only when the Difference's left operand is not compatibility-selection-safe or a shared name is not assured on its right operand.

Wrong results (3.4.4 as designed): a planner-emitted minus-assured-shared Filter that is variable-scope-changed, nested in an EXISTS body, has a VALUES left operand, or arrives with only the kind hint is still evaluated with NOT EXISTS substitution (e.g. `?s :p ?o MINUS { ?s :q ?v FILTER(?v = ?o) }` drops rows that MINUS keeps).

Wrong results, pre-existing and copied into the new residual (3.4.1/3.9): `?s :p ?o LATERAL { OPTIONAL { ?s :q ?y FILTER(?y = ?o) } }` never matches because ?o is scoped out of the LeftJoin condition.

Perf (3.4.3): Projection-rooted EXISTS bodies keep per-probe unbound evaluation until follow-up (d); LIMIT/aggregate sub-selects that were (incorrectly) bind-joined per outer row now run the full body once per probe.
verifiedClaims: 3.4.1 root cause: LeftJoinQueryEvaluationStep.java:95 is the only independent (hash) path and requires !hasCondition(); with a condition supply returns `standard` (:131) whose evaluate (:166-181) uses LeftJoinIterator, which calls rightEvaluationStep.evaluate(leftBindings) per left row (LeftJoinIterator.java:94,103); ProjectionQueryEvaluationStep.java:37 forwards the whole row into the sub-select; GroupIterator.java:299 evaluates aggregate arguments with parentBindings. develop (4354ff137b^2 :46-53) returned HashJoinIteration unconditionally for a sub-select RHS and dropped the condition.

TupleExprs.containsSubquery stops at the first Join (TupleExprs.java:57-62) and JoinQueryEvaluationStep guards only its right arg (:80, :159-177), so a sub-select as the LEFT arg of a Join inside OPTIONAL is evaluated with the correlated row (the design's 'containsSubquery-stops-at-Join hole').

3.4.2 root cause: MinusQueryEvaluationStep passes the full input bindings to the right operand both via DelayedEvaluationIteration (:97) and AdaptiveMinusIteration.initialize (:254), while comparisonBindingNames are shared output names (:104-137) and SPARQLMinusIteration compares only bound names in the comparison domain (:99-105, :255-274). The memory repro `minusInsideOptionalIsEvaluatedIndependently` is fixed by either 3.4.1 (hash) or 3.4.2 alone.

3.4.3 root cause: evaluateSubstitutedExists (FilterIterator.java:361-369) runs BindingAssignerOptimizer, whose VarVisitor replaces every bound Var with no scope awareness (BindingAssignerOptimizer.java:45-52); it is reached from both DefaultEvaluationStrategy.prepare(Exists) (:2112-2129) and the semi-join path (:303-304) for every non-selection-safe body (:442-475 excludes Projection/Slice/Group).

3.4.4 root cause: assuredSharedMinus only relaxes the root scope-change check (FilterIterator.java:249-256); requiresPerProbeExistsSubstitution (:257) forces STREAMING with full-row substitution; correlationCandidates/materializationParameterNames include every referenced var (:265-280). The planner emits the hint only when shared names are assured on both sides (PackedLogicalRuleProgram.java:386-391) and stamps the kind on both the ANTI_JOIN form (PackedPlanMaterializer.java:255-273) and the FILTER form (PackedCostSession.java:490-495), so the executor's validation definition (outputs∩outputs, assured both sides) matches the planner's. PhysicalOperatorReviewReproTest#minusAssuredSharedHint... does exercise :249-369 (QueryRoot parent, streaming hint, Filter body).

3.4.5a: HashJoinIteration.java:145-146 opens both inputs in the constructor with no guard; handleClose (:264-311) cannot run; callers JoinQueryEvaluationStep.java:77/83, LeftJoinQueryEvaluationStep.java:98, FederationEvaluationStrategy.java:823 and BoundedHashJoinIteration (:670) all use that constructor. The repro hashJoinClosesLeftWhenRightEvaluationFails hits exactly this constructor.

3.4.5b: setupHashTable/drain (:344-375) buffer the whole build input into an unbounded ArrayList (makeIterationCache :657-659); only BoundedHashJoinIteration (:665-687) bounds it. Deferral is reasonable.

Hash-join compatibility claims: HashJoinBindingContract.from gives lookup = assured∩assured and compatibility = possible∩possible (HashJoinBindingContract.java from()); build rows missing a lookup attribute go to partial-key indexes (HashJoinIteration.java:410-421) and probe rows missing attributes scan all rows with a compatibility check (:528-531), so nullable shared bindings cannot drop rows.

3.9-lateral trace: lateral-02.rq and LateralTest#testLateralWithOptional (LateralTest.java:108-114) are the same query; tests() lists LateralWithOptional second (:588-590); manifest-all includes aggregates (4 QueryEvaluationTests) before lateral. rightInputBindingNames = enclosing inputs ∪ left binding names = {s,o} (TupleExprBuilder.java:3266-3277). The LeftJoin's optionalVars {s,label} are not reduced because the SingletonSet left has no binding names (LeftJoinQueryEvaluationStep.java:142-158); input {s,o} -> isWellDesignedFor false -> BadlyDesignedLeftJoinIterator evaluates left and right without s (:73,:131), LIMIT 1 returns the store's first label, the compatibility check (:85) rejects it for other subjects and no bare left row is emitted -> 1 row. The cloned right arg has no parent (LateralQueryEvaluationStep.java:101-104); `SELECT *` keeps s as a projected source so the renamer does not hide it. Excluding {s,o} from optionalVars alone (before 3.4.1/3.4.3) already fixes the test via the existing hash branch.

Parser scope-change marking: only UNION branches are flagged (ASTUnionGraphPattern.java:20; TupleExprBuilder.java:1466-1467, 1548), OPTIONAL groups are not, so `isVariableScopeChange` in the LeftJoin predicate does not route every OPTIONAL to hash (but does route every UNION-in-OPTIONAL; see issue).

BindingAssignerOptimizer runs first in both the standard pipeline (StandardQueryOptimizerPipeline.java:72) and the LMDB pipeline (LmdbQueryOptimizerPipeline.java:245), so external bindings are constants before evaluation in both stores; the top-level pass-through guard in 3.4.3 is load-bearing only for FedX/direct strategy callers. LmdbEvaluationStrategy does not override Projection/LeftJoin precompilation.

3.4.1 badly-designed wrapper (c): BadlyDesignedLeftJoinIterator's compatibility filter + problem-var re-extension (:84-106) and getFilteredBindings (:181-185) are self-contained and can wrap the hash step; LeftJoinQueryEvaluationStepTest#badlyDesignedOptionalDeclinesIndependentEvaluationAlgorithms (Projection case, :95-125 via assertBottomUpSemantics :584-612) asserts only the empty result, so it stays green with the wrapper. #subqueryOptionalWith{FalseCondition,ConditionError}DeclinesHashJoin (:654-690) assert LeftJoinIterator at :684 and will need the HashJoinIteration expectation as the design says.

MaterializedExistsFilterIteration mechanics used by 3.4.4: materialization bindings come only from materializationParameterBindingNames (:298-302), matches() compares only sharedBindingNames with wildcard handling (:389-437), so with shared assured on both sides and empty parameters the MATERIALIZED mode is exactly MINUS compatibility on assured shared names.
